question: On two fixed development failure prefixes, does one uniform cached sibling before native repair improve first accepted valid submission within the same wall budget?
scope: Exploratory conditioned repair episode, not full search, not a held-out confirmation
layout: Two dedicated 2-GPU generator services and two 1-GPU MLE workers on gpu28; crossover arm-to-lane assignment in second pair
controls: same original operators and ancestor memory
same public data and initial error
same resource reservation and stopping rule
stopping: Stop on first native accepted submission or episode deadline or max debug depth. In-flight work is killed at common deadline; it cannot become a late incumbent. No truncated-answer salvage. Cache failure falls back to the original failed prefix, not the failed sibling.
measurement: Whole episode clock includes imports, public preview, generation, program execution, native analysis, and cleanup. Generator startup excluded from episode but all allocation GPU-hours reported. No external score or validity provided to the model; external validation and grading after all episodes close.
limitations: Both prefixes and cache outcomes already seen in development
two physical runs, not four independent trials
shared generation sunk cost conditional on existing pool; does not prove full-search savings
local native-operator loop rather than resumed production checkpoint
fresh isolated code execution workspaces in both arms
node-wide contention possible despite dedicated GPU/CPU partitions
